correctness.rationale: The deterministic burst output collision equivalence is proved by direct string alignment. For uniformly proper words, independent nonzero modular increments yield stationary b-dependent return indicators. The complete-graph transition-matrix spectrum provides return and joint-return probabilities; an explicitly factored covariance kernel yields exact all-n moments and strict sign claims. For b=2 the constraints on successive increments form a path with sequentially constant conditional match probabilities, giving independent Bernoulli indicators. A separated-block Lindeberg argument proves the fixed-b CLT. Independent brute-force string-output enumeration and exact rational moments passed 108 strata, q=2..4 and n<=9.

value.rationale: Homopolymer-free strings are an important proper-word constraint for constrained coding; the natural number of distinct possible burst-erasure outputs controls channel ambiguity. Exact all-length dispersion and a fixed-b Gaussian fluctuation coefficient materially extend earlier worst-case and unconstrained binary counts. The clean independence-to-correlation transition at b=2 vs b>=3 is a structural boundary that matters for distributional approximation and cannot be inferred from an ordinary unconstrained binary binomial model alone.
